\smallskip
\begin{minipage}{\linewidth}\scriptsize\raggedright
Medians over the instances (CG iterations, from the zero field / to the prediction's accuracy, and CG's displacement error: over the load cases). 2D: the first 32 validation instances of the two-dimensional comparison; 3D: the first 32 validation and 8 fine-mesh instances of the three-dimensional comparison; the label-free transformers of seed 0. Wall times per instance, all load cases together, without the assembly, which the surrogate does not need.\par
Surrogate: one NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 with TF32, preparing the inputs and copying the prediction back included; first call after an untimed warm-up on 4 validation instances, repeated call the median of 2 further passes. Solvers: the CPU of the same machine (Xeon Platinum 8470Q, 25 CPUs, the thread environment set to 25): SuperLU, which produced the labels, and unpreconditioned conjugate gradients (CG) to a relative residual of $10^{-10}$, from the zero field or from the prediction. CG to the prediction's accuracy stops, on each load case, at the first iterate whose relative energy error is at most the prediction's: it reads the reference solution, a lower bound. The fine-mesh direct solve used up its budget of 900 s after seven of the eight instances; its median, and the ratios that use it, are over those seven.\par
Ritz projection (\cref{sec:methods:ritz}), from the lowest to the highest degree ($p = 6$ to 9 in 3D, 6 and 8 in 2D), with the machine's 25 BLAS threads: the time after the assembly of $K$, which is listed apart (in 2D the assembler also builds the four load vectors), for the free block, the basis, $\Phi^{\top}K\Phi$ and $\Phi^{\top}F$, the small solve and the reconstruction.\par
On the fine mesh, three of the 32 load cases had a relative energy gap above 1 (4.76, 4.77 and 22.0) and three of the eight instances a mean above 1; CG matches such a load case with no iteration. Threads: \cref{sec:cost:inference} and the supplementary material.
\end{minipage}
